Description: We propose to provide an organized, documented, and transparent archive of planetary mission data for the science community and general public worldwide through the continued operation of NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS) atmospheres node at new mexico state university. the atmospheres node (atm) will maximize NASA's return on its investment in planetary exploration and will aid in the expansion of knowledge of all communities. our team is uniquely qualified to provide this service to the planetary science community due to our collective expertise in planetary atmospheres, our role in the development of pds4, our history in working with missions and individual data providers, and our proposed initiatives for improving data discoverability and interoperability. the mission data we will curate in the atmospheres node (atm) consist of historical data already in the atm archive, data from current missions that are actively archiving at atm, and data from future missions with at least one instrument that will yield atmospheric science data. the historical and current mission data comprise an archive approximately 38 TB in size, arising from missions to every planet in the SOLAR system and acquired over a time period of more than 40 years. the future data we will archive will likely double the size of the atmos holdings and will be provided BY MRO, MAVEN, curiosity, insight, juno, perseverance, europa clipper, and atmospheric components of yet To Be Determined discovery and/or new frontiers missions. in addition, we will archive a range of ground-based telescopic, laboratory, and field data acquired in support of NASA missions AS well AS a variety of derived or higher order data products. in addition to the ongoing work with current and future mission teams, the other primary atmospheres node activities for the proposed award period will include: - migrating the atm data holdings that remain in pds3 to the more modern pds4 standards - working with individual data providers to efficiently archive their data products - expanding the development of the educational labeling system at atmospheres, a pds4 label template generator, to include a broader range of filetypes - obtaining dois for all atm data holdings to improve their citability and discoverability - developing and implementing a cloud computing strategy for atm that is aligned with PDS cloud computing roadmap - working with an external entity on atm website design and management - ensuring that the atm it systems are secure while maintaining data integrity in the atm archives - enhancing communication with our user community and ensuring accessibility of the atm data archives
